sections.text: Lord Shri Krishna said: Now, O Prince! Listen to My supreme advice, which I give thee for the sake of thy welfare, for thou art My beloved.
न मे विदुः सुरगणाः प्रभवं न महर्षयः।
Neither the professors of divinity nor the great ascetics know My origin, for I am the source of them all.
He who knows Me as the unborn, without beginning, the Lord of the universe, he, stripped of his delusion, becomes free from all conceivable sin.

So we completed chapter nine and well now be discussing chapter 10, Vibhuti yoga. In the first six chapters we learned about I, the limited being which is part of this prakriti. Prakriti has three constituent parts: Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas.
Everything in this Prakriti is made up of these three Gunas; whichever has the predominance, that becomes my nature. Sattva is purity, Rajas is activity, and Tamas is inertia. Everything in this prakriti is made up of these three gunas, and we have learned the nature of Prakriti in chapter seven.
Up to chapter six we learnt about us as the limited beings and the makeup of our beings. From chapter 7 onward, we are learning about the nature of the supreme, the Lord. In chapter seven we learnt about his lower natures.
Bhagavan said this Ashtadha Prakriti: Bhumi, Apah, Analaha, Kham, Vayu, Mana, Buddhi, Ahankara. The eight , five great elements, Mind, intellect, and Ahankara , are the nature of prakriti, my lower nature. These are not different from me, but they are my lower nature in the sense of the grosser manifestation which you and I can perceive through our senses.
We discussed Prakriti in chapter seven. Chapter eight said that in Prakriti, things are unmanifest in the beginning, then manifest in the middle, then unmanifest again. So Prakriti itself has two aspects.
One is manifest, one is unmanifest. There is unmanifest, Prakriti. There is manifest Prakriti.
Bhagawan said, other than this unmanifest, there is another unmanifest which is my higher. Prakriti, which always remains unmanifest, is the support of all things and beings. So in chapter 8, Akshara Brahma yoga, we learnt about this unmanifest nature of Purusha remaining unmanifest, it supports everything.
Bhagawan said that Im the origin of all things and beings and Im also the dissolution of all things and beings. I get confused about my being and therefore Im not experiencing the very nature of the supreme. The very nature of the supreme is Sat-Chit-Ananda , Sat is existence, Chit is knowledge, and Ananda is happiness or bliss.
So right now Im not truly experiencing Sat. I know I exist, but Im afraid Ill become non-existent. Im not experiencing Sat fully.
I know something, but I dont know everything, so Im not experiencing Chit either. And Ananda is my biggest problem. Happiness comes and goes.
For a while Im happy, and most of the time Im just pursuing happiness. So Im trying to get out of the impermanent nature of Ananda into the permanent nature of Ananda, trying to find out where that permanent Ananda is. Bhagavan in the ninth chapter says thats the royal secret, the greatest secret: it is your very nature to be Sat-Chit-Ananda, but you are not experiencing it.
That knowledge which connects me back to my real nature is the royal knowledge. So that was chapter nine. At the end of chapter nine, Bhagavan said the only way one can experience this is Manmana Bhava.
Make your mind focused on me. Offer yourself to me. Make me as your goal Yuktva Mat Parayanaha.
In other words, completely identify with me and you will experience that Ananda which you are seeking. Now how do I get to that level where I can completely identify with him is the subject of chapter 10. So its called Vibhuti Yoga.
Yoga of divine glories. I see, perceive, touch and feel this world of my experiences. But I break them all down into perishable things and beings.
Anything which I see, I can say I understand this. This is just a table. All this, I understand this.
Well, I understand this is plant kingdom. So I break this down into the impermanent, perishable conglomeration of things and beings which by very nature they are impermanent and not divine. I dont consider them as divine.
I dont say this table is divine. I dont consider my colleagues as divine. Even when some wise person comes.
But he is not Bhagavan. We have difficulty if somebody calls himself Bhagawan because we cannot associate the divinity with the objects of my perception. So how to change that and start seeing Divinity in everything I see and touch and feel is the subject of chapter 10.
Therefore it is called Yoga of Divine Glory. How to see this divinity, this divine glories in everything and being that I come across in the world of my experiences, my world of my perception. So Bhagavan starts this chapter without waiting for Arjuna to ask questions because he saw that he is enjoying it and he wanted to continue the theme which he started in chapter seven about the Prakriti.
When he says, this Prakriti is nothing but my lower nature. Everything in this Prakriti Aa Sesah. There is nothing left in this Prakriti which is not divine.
But we dont really see that way. In fact, we divide this world into good and evil. We have some level of acceptance that good is divine.
But we are difficult when it comes to bad and ugly. I cant associate divinity with it. This chapter will say that even that is only possible.
Bad is only possible because of my presence and evil is only possible because of my presence. There is nothing that can happen or exist in this world without me. So chapter opens with Bhagavans statement says Bhuya Eva Mahabaho srunume paramam vacha yatta te aham Priyamanaya vakshyami Hita Kamya.
I wish your welfare Hita Kamiya. Therefore Im going to continue. And in last chapter I told you that this knowledge is available to all.
And we discussed that verse which is very troublesome to discuss and say. Those who are born in Papayonayaha Triya vaishya tathakshadraha. Even they have equal right when they come to me.
If they focus their mind onto me. We discuss why Papayoni. Anything which takes me away from my identification with the supreme is sin.
That which does not recognize my true potential which is Sat chit in Ananda is Papa. It is the impurity on my mind which is right now not letting me see who I am. An environment which is more likely to create wrong impressions on my mind is Papa Yoni.
Yoni is a collection of people which creates an environment that is similar for each other , a symbiotic relationship. Its like a satsang in reverse , bad company. If Im put in that environment where I get more sinful impressions on my mind, I have less chance of rising out of it.
Even those people who are disadvantaged by their environment , those who are put in a society that does not give them the equal right to achieve what they try to achieve , can still rise above that. Triya Vaishya Tatakshudra. Interestingly, the Vaishyas never complained about this verse.
Only two groups complain. Vaishya didnt say why we are included in it as well. We are higher than you now.
All business people are worshipped now, not Kshatriyas and Brahmanas. So Bhagawan says that at the time of Mahabharata, Vaishyas were not considered as high as the Brahmins and Kshatriyas. I heard when I was growing up.
Which profession you are supposed to take? Uttam Kheti Keti Farming. Madhyam Vyapa and Kanishta Nokri. The worst is you want to work for somebody is Kanishta.
We all work for corporate and feel great about it. If you cant do farming then only you do Vaipa. So they were considered lower in that society.
Now today in India, if you tell someone to become a farmer , how many farmers are committing suicide? Why would you want me to do farming? But in that society, Kshatriyas were farmers. Janakaraj, when he was tilling his land, found Sita. Kshatriyas, the kings, were themselves landlords and farmers.
So those people in that environment had a great chance to uplift themselves by getting this knowledge. But others did not have those equal rights. Women, Vaishya, Kshudra.
But even they can get this knowledge and come to me. But you are a Mahabaho. You are the mighty armed person who has all the opportunities and all the prerequisites to know this.
So Bhuya Eva Mahabaho again. Listen to my very important words. I think you have come to a level that you are understanding what Im saying.
Manmana Bhava Madh Bhakta Madhya ji Mam namaskaru. I heard Obama saying the other day, stay focused. Dont get distracted by the protesters.
Dont get distracted by your doubts in your mind. Bhagavan says Paramam vacha yate aham Priyamanaya. And Im only telling those people who likes to listen to this type of knowledge.
Vakshyami Hitakami Ayyaa. Because I wish welfare for you all. And therefore Im telling you.
So what Im telling you is what we had started in the last chapter saying. What is the royal secret? Aham Adhi Devanam Maharshinam Chasarva Sah. Neither the Devas in the heavens nor the great Rishis know my origin.
What is the source of my being? Not on the great Rishis, not the Devas. Because even in Puranas, Devas have their own limitations. Devas are considered pretty greedy.
They want to have everything. Devas, they dont know. And Rishis, they are distracted by their own intellect.
See, when we learn something, we get to a level where our intellect will become an obstacle. We cant experience it because we keep doubting ourselves. So Bhagavan says, even they dont know.
Because the source of the Deva and Rishis is me. Dheeranandas very famous example. Batteries in the flashlight.
If youre in a dark room and I have flashlight, I can see everything in the room. But somebody says, what type of batteries are you using, Rajan? I say, well, let me take it out. I take out the batteries.
I put the batteries back. Light is back, but I cant see the batteries. I said, I dont know till tomorrow morning.
So the source of the light in the flashlight is the batteries. And therefore I cannot know through the light of the flashlight the type of batteries Im using. Through my intellect, which is the Rishi, I cannot know the source of my being.
I constantly try to contemplate through my intellect by deduction and inferences who I am. Bhagavan said, you will not know that the Rishis, our intellect, the knower, the seer in us is the Rishi. In the Devas are our sense perceptions.
To illumine something which is illuminated by my senses. So my senses are the Devas. Without them, the world is not existent for me.
You remove the one sense of seeing. The world of sight is gone. You remove the hearing.
The world of sound is gone. You remove all five senses. The world is illuminated by my senses.
So they are Devas through my senses. I am trying to find Bhagavan. I want to see Bhagavan.
I want to see the presence of Bhagavan. In the laboratory, when somebody dies, what happens? Where is that atma is going? The people have done experiments of people dying. And what is it that leaving they cannot find it simply because Bhagavan said, because I am the source of this Deva Dhanda, I am the source of your senses and your intellect.
You will never be able to find me through this. Because the instrument cannot find its own source. Bhagwan says, aham, Adhi Diwanam, Maharishi Nam Cha Sarvasa.
Im not available to any of those, to the sense perceptions or by intellectual inquiry. Im only available by contemplation and identification. By identification that I will be able to find myself.
Yom Ajam Anadim Chavaiyati. One who knows that I am that I. Whichever way you apply it, when applied to the supreme, he is the God.
Bhagawan says I , that includes everything.

Krishna declares that neither the celestial beings (Devas) nor the great sages (Maharishis) can fully comprehend His origin, for He is the source of them all. This teaching invites us to a profound humility: the instruments we use to understand reality - our senses and intellect - are themselves products of that supreme reality. Just as batteries in a flashlight cannot illuminate themselves, our mind and senses cannot fully grasp their own source. Yet knowing Him as unborn, beginningless, and Lord of the universe liberates us from delusion and all conceivable sin.
Consider how you typically try to figure out the divine through analysis and reasoning. These verses suggest that intellectual understanding alone has limits - the knower cannot fully objectify its own source. Instead, Krishna offers this knowledge out of love (priyamanaya - to one who is dear) and for our welfare (hitakamyaya). Today, practice approaching spiritual understanding not as a puzzle to solve, but as a relationship to deepen. When you encounter something beyond your comprehension - a moment of unexpected grace, an inexplicable feeling of peace, the mystery of consciousness itself - instead of immediately trying to analyze it, allow yourself to simply rest in not-knowing.
Ask yourself: How would my daily life change if I truly accepted that my mind cannot fully grasp its own source? What would it mean to approach the divine with the heart of a beloved, rather than only the intellect of an investigator?
